title: pvResampleToLine
body:
## pvResampleToLine

Same native filter as pvPlotOverLine (vtkPVProbeLineFilter) with a different starting configuration: uniform sampling with Resolution 40 and the SamplingPattern hidden in ParaView's GUI. It returns a polyline with the input arrays interpolated along Point1-Point2 plus arc_length and vtkValidPointMask. Use it for a light uniform resampling, e.g. a coarse profile to compare between runs; use pvPlotOverLine or probeLine for detailed profiles.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Omitted, Point1 and Point2 are never the static [0, 0, 0]: in a bounded native probe with a polydata upstream a batch run read (1, 1, 1) and (-1, -1, -1), a line unrelated to the data (composite inputs give other uninitialised-bounds corners, by the source), and when the upstream already had data they were the corners of its bounding box. Always set both.
- Points outside the data are flagged by vtkValidPointMask 0; exclude them before computing statistics.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `ResampleToLine`. Identity: `filters/ResampleToLine`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies which data set to resample. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); composite data (multiblock or partitioned collections) (vtkCompositeDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). The input needs at least one point- or cell-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkCompositeDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeTolerance` | Set whether to compute the tolerance or to use a user provided value. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassCellArrays` | When set the input cell data arrays are shallow copied to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassFieldArrays` | Set whether to pass the field-data arrays from the Input i.e. the input providing the geometry to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassPartialArrays` | When dealing with composite datasets, partial arrays are common i.e. data-arrays that are not available in all of the blocks. By default, this filter only passes those point and cell data-arrays that are available in all the blocks i.e. partial arrays are removed. When PassPartialArrays is turned on, this behavior is changed to take a union of all arrays present thus partial arrays are passed as well. However, for composite dataset input, this filter still produces a non-composite output. For all those locations in a block of where a particular data array is missing, this filter uses vtkMath::Nan() for double and float arrays, and 0 for all other types of arrays i.e int, char etc. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassPointArrays` | When set the input point data arrays are shallow copied to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Point1` | This property controls the coordinates of the first endpoint of the line. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Point2` | This property controls the coordinates of the second endpoint of the line. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Resolution` | This property sets the line resolution. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `SamplingPattern` | How sample points are placed on the line. Sample Uniformly spaces Resolution samples evenly, which smooths over cell structure; Sample At Cell Boundaries puts a pair of points at every cell crossing so cell data appear as exact steps (most faithful); Sample At Segment Centers gives one sample per crossed cell, convenient for cell-wise tables. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Sample At Cell Boundaries","Sample At Segment Centers","Sample Uniformly"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Sample At Cell Boundaries"` |
| `Tolerance` | Set the tolerance to use for vtkDataSet::FindCell | `{"minimum":2.220446049250313e-16,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `2.220446049250313e-16` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvResampleToLine",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
